chunks: Describing your rework experience. The question: Describe any rework experience you have.
The interviewer is asking, "Have you really fixed a circuit board, and what did you learn?" They are not checking a fact.
They want a short true story that shows you can find out what is wrong before touching anything, handle the repair carefully, and think about why the problem happened.
Even a small job makes a good story if you give real detail.
A good answer is a tiny detective story.
Something was broken, you looked for clues, you made the fix, you checked that it worked, and you worked out how to stop it happening again.
A weak answer skips the detective work and only says "I used a soldering iron." One honest slip-up in the story sounds more real than a story where nothing went wrong.
A rework story is a diagnosis story with a soldering step in the middle. Interviewers follow your reasoning along this chain; weak answers contain only the "Action" box.
Rework: removing, replacing or changing parts on a board that is already built. STAR: a story shape: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
Diagnosis: finding out which part or connection is the problem, usually by measuring, before you fix anything.
Root cause: the real reason the fault happened, not just the broken part you replaced. Verification: checking after the fix that the board really works.
Here is a skeleton to fill in with your own true details. "On my [project] , the [symptom] showed up. I measured [what you measured] and narrowed it to [the part] .
I replaced it using [your tools and method] . It did not go perfectly: [one honest slip and how you recovered] . I checked it by [how you verified] .
The root cause was [why it failed] , so I [what you changed so it will not recur] ." If your experience is small, say so. Never claim work you did not do. That is the whole idea.
"On my [project] board, a [part] failed, so I diagnosed it with a multimeter and thermal camera, then replaced it with a hot-air station: flux, preheat, low airflow, Kapton on the neighbours.
I lifted a pad on the first attempt, patched it with a wire, and learned to wait until every joint is liquid.
Afterwards I checked under the microscope, re-measured the rail, and fixed the footprint error that caused the failure."
Quick check. What is the main purpose of preheating the board before hot-air rework?
